title: Teams, Shifts and Certificates, All in One Place: Open Source Volunteer and Shift Management
description:
**How do you build a feature for a real open-source project when the codebase, requirements, and users already exist?**

In this lightning talk, I’ll share my journey building **TeamShifts**, a team and volunteer management plugin for FOSSASIA’s **Eventyay** platform as part of **Google Summer of Code 2026**.

The plugin brings **calls for team members, roles, applications, shift scheduling, team assignments, certifications, and volunteer vouchers** into the event-management platform instead of relying on separate tools.

I’ll give a quick look at how the project evolved from **understanding an existing Django codebase** to designing the plugin architecture, integrating it with Eventyay, building the application workflow, and working through GitHub issues, pull requests, code reviews, and mentor feedback.

Rather than being just a feature walkthrough, this talk is a practical look at **what it is like to contribute to a real open-source project **— from understanding someone else’s code and making design decisions to handling reviews and collaborating with maintainers and other contributors.

**I’ll also share a few practical lessons from the journey:**

- Working effectively in an existing codebase

- Turning requirements into features in an open-source project

- Learning through code reviews and mentor feedback

- Finding your place and contributing as a new open-source contributor
